$doc: The profiler's records and sections as the core lays them out and the client reads
them from the replies that hand them over (perf/record.rs, ts/client/src/service/core/perf.ts):
word offsets, eight bytes a word. The names the numbers index are their owners':
a task's io's (spec/client/core/sys/io/demand.json), a step's and an effect's the
turn's (spec/client/core/turn/step.json), a GPU span's the renderer's
(spec/client/render/gpu/span.json). A packed table gives each field's
width and the generator lays the offsets out. Nothing is built
for a read: the core writes numbers where they stay, and the words for them are
the UI's. LIMIT holds the bounds the profiler keeps, and the one a build made for
measuring hands its GPU runtimes, which the core and the client both read.
$HIT_KINDS: What the pick met (NOW.view `hit_kind`; pxl-core domain/query/ray.rs `HitKind`): the ground, a placed cube, placed cubes folded into a coarser box, or a decor.

LIMIT.$REASON_WORDS: A reason's words: its fail, its detail and how many (STREAM_STAT.reasons).
LIMIT.$WINDOW_MS: How far back the rings keep, the core's frames and tasks and the UI's long frames alike: the last minute.
LIMIT.$PAGE_BYTES: The most bytes one read of a ring hands over (perf.wit `rings`): a ring is read a page at a time, each from where the last ended, until a page comes short. The string table and the statistics fit one page.
LIMIT.$SLOW_MS: In a build made for measuring, the runtimes say a record of the GPU stream, the stream's run or the core's turn slower than this, the page's and the device's alike (xpute-gpu `CoreConfig::slow_ms`, @xpute/gpu `GpuConfig`, @xpute/runtime `Config`).

$doc: One frame and the interval it opened (perf/frame.rs FrameSample): every figure of one frame, landed when the next frame closes the interval. `interval_ms` is that interval, `refresh_ms` the display's measured interval (pxl-core sys/sched/display.rs), and `paced_ms` the gap since the last frame, which the frame was paced at (pxl-core turn.rs `world_frame`). `settled` is 1 where the frame asked for no next one, else 0. `effects_ms`, `tick_ms` and `stage_ms` are the frame's parts, `stage_ms` the requests' pump and the render, and `perf_ms` what the profiler cost it, its own record of the frame and the UI's reads of it. `effects` is each effect's time in the frame turn, in EFFECT_NAMES' order, `effects_ms` their sum. `gpu_timed` is 1 where the GPU's read of this frame has landed, which comes a frame or two later and is written back into this frame's record (`gpu_frame` the renderer's number of it, 0 where it drew none): its `gpu_spans` are then that read's, `gpu_busy_ms` the time they ran, those that overlap counted once, the frame's GPU time, which the spans' sum overstates where passes overlap (pxl-render gpu/api.rs `Gpu::gpu_busy_ms`), and `gpu_px` the world's pixels of the frame the read timed, what the spans were measured over; and 0 where nothing measured it (its read not landed yet or cut off by a stop, or the device keeps no timestamps), its spans, busy time and pixels 0 too. `scale` is the share of the display's pixels, each way, the world was drawn at, in every frame (pxl-core domain/scene/resolution.rs `drawn_scale`). `kind_name` indexes the renderer's FRAME_KINDS. `draws` and `triangles` are the frame's, every pipeline a draw names (pxl-render gpu/draw.rs `DRAW_PIPELINES`), counted while the profiler records. `light_changed` says what changed that cast the light's map in the frame, a bit each in LIGHT_CHANGED's order (pxl-render ray/cast.rs `light_changed`), 0 where it did not cast; `decor_rects` is how many rects decor's slots were marked by to generate again in it, the bricks handed in it and the edits and cuts held (pxl-render gpu/generator.rs `prepare`), 0 where it marked none. The ray columns are the `ray_cnts` setting's, written into the frame they were counted in as the counts land a frame or two later, by the renderer's number of it as a GPU read is (pxl-render ray/count.rs `RayCount`), 0 where none landed: `eye_cast` and `light_cast` 1 where the eye cast in full or the light's map cast and its counts landed; then the eye's pixels (`eye_rays`) and the light's map's slots (`light_rays`), and an observer's each: the nodes its beam rays, its samples and its holes' walk visited (`_beam`, `_sample`, `_hole_walk`), the asks of the world among the last (`_asks`), its pixels or slots that took the visible voxel, a walk of their own as holes and the sky (`_voxel`, `_hole`, `_sky`), together every one it cast again, so the light's three over `light_rays` are the share of its map a cast cast again, and the boxes drawn (pxl-engine `count`). `terrain_loads` is how many terrain tiles the tile cache took in during the frame turn (pxl-core domain/layer/tile_cache.rs `take_loads`). `uploads` and `uploads_bytes` are the renderer's upload table and `pack_bytes` its texture pack (pxl-render renderer.rs `FrameStat`), and `heap_used_bytes` the heap's high-water mark (pxl-core sys/heap.rs `HeapStat`). A column's name says its unit: `_ms`, `_bytes`, `_px`, and `_name` for an index into a list of names.

FRAME's columns in groups, every column in one (column.test.ts), in the order a reader asks in turn — where the time went, what was drawn and cast, what landed, and what it holds. The trace prints every column by its group's order, so a column the core adds is printed without a word written for it; the panel shows some groups, a few rows each, and the report its own lines. The `rays` group's columns lie in FRAME in its order, which the window's sums of them (STAT.frames.rays) keep.

One settled task (perf/task.rs TaskRecord). `path` is the bytes of the path it opened, zero past their end, and every other word an f64; `start_ms` is NaN for a task that never ran; `stream`, `outcome` and each of `phase_ids` index STREAM_NAMES, OUTCOME_NAMES and TASK_PHASE_NAMES. `at_file` is the offset of the file name, `at_file_bytes` long, of the line a failure was made at, in the string table PERF_STRTAB hands over, or 0 where the table had no room for the name, whose `at_line` is kept; every site word is 0 where the failure was the runtime's.

One of the worst moving frames since the recording started, by its interval, and what changed from the frame before it: its uploads, their bytes and the heap's high-water mark, each this frame's less that one's, all 0 where `has_prev` is 0. A still interval is long on purpose and is never among them.
A value's percentiles over n values: p50 and p95 each the nearest rank, the least value at or above which lie no more than that share of the n (sorted, the value at ceil(q × n) − 1), and the most.
One stream's tasks in the window, at STAT.tasks.slots + its index × WORDS. Each reason is (fail, detail, n), commonest first; `phase_mean` is NaN for a phase no task reported.
One registered step's timing, at STAT.steps.slots + its index × WORDS. `name` indexes STEP_NAMES.

The window's statistics PERF_STATS computes, over its `window_ms`: each section's words at its AT, the fields relative to it. Every word an f64. Packed: a section's AT is where the one before it ends, and WORDS where the last ends, both laid out by the generator.

What the frames held at the most or the least since the recording started, as the steps are timed, folded as each frame turn's record is taken (perf/record.rs `perf_fold_recording`): `frames` the frame turns folded; the heap's figures by their allocator's names (pxl-core sys/heap.rs `HeapStat`), the most of each but `largest_free`, the least, and `refusals` as it last stood; the body slots' peak (sys/io/body.rs `take_peak`); and `terrain_refusals` the terrain tiles the tile cache refused a slot, summed (domain/layer/tile_cache.rs `take_refusals`). Every word 0 before a frame is folded.
What PERF_STATS finds as it reads, the window aside: each section's words at its AT, as STAT lays out its own. Every word an f64.

Whether it records, how long the recording has run, whether it lost what it had no room for (a ring's oldest records, or a failure's file name the string table could not hold), and how many records each ring holds (RING_NAMES).

Whether the core draws, as the read finds it, recording or not, every count since the core booted: `frames` the frames the renderer encoded (pxl-render renderer.rs `drawn_frames`); `refused_admit` and `refused_stream` the frames that did not run, as the GPU admitted none (xpute-gpu admit) or the runtime still held the stream (xpute-core ipc/stream.rs R3) (turn.rs `frame_task`).

Then the device, as the runtime wrote its block (xpute spec DEVICE), the same on a page and on a device: `generation` the devices lost so far (pxl-render gpu/api.rs `device_generation`); `status` its STATUS, 0 before the block is written; `errors` the uncaptured errors it raised; and `unfinished` the frames whose work its queue has not done, each a frame the runtime asked the queue to say done and has not heard of.

Where the camera, its pivot and the pointer are as the read finds them, recording or not: `eye_x`..`eye_z`, `dist`, `pivot_x`..`pivot_z`, `hover_x`..`hover_z` and `place_x`..`place_z` in units, angles in radians, `pivot_lon` and `pivot_lat` in degrees and `pivot_alt` in meters, a zoom as its number, and NaN where there is none.

The eye is where the camera looks from and the pivot the point it turns about, the eye itself in the first-person camera, where the character stands (pxl-core domain/control/camera.rs `eye_world`, camera/controller.rs `pivot`).

The hover is what the pointer meets, exactly, at the zooms the eye's rays ask, whatever the tool could strike, and `cell_zoom` the zoom the eye's rays draw there (pxl-core domain/query/ray.rs `by_dist`).

The pick is what the tool held strikes there (pxl-core domain/control/edit/pick.rs `pick_at`): `hit_kind` what it met, an index into HIT_KINDS; `pick_zoom` the zoom of the box struck and `ray_zoom` the rays' there, `folded` 1 where they draw coarser than the box, which strikes nothing. `place_x`..`place_z` is the corner the tool takes (pxl-core domain/control/edit.rs `Hover`), `place_zoom` the zoom it places at, and `blocked` 1 where that room is taken (domain/control/edit/collision.rs `is_placement_blocked`).

$RING_NAMES: The rings the profiler keeps: the frames, the tasks, and the worst moving frames since the recording started.
